guardrails.title: Guardrails
guardrails.subtitle: What your assistants may never do, and the scenarios that check it.

rules.title: What the assistant must never do
rules.desc: Every rule applies to ALL your assistants. Nothing is fixed: add, edit or remove.

fixtures.title: Scenarios
fixtures.desc: Real exchanges replayed against the assistant before activating it — "what if they write STOP?", "what if they ask a price?".

core.title: Base instructions
core.desc: The shared text given to all your assistants: who they are, what they may not say, how they write.

reset.confirmBody: “{label}” will revert to its default configuration. This happens immediately.

resetAll.confirmBody: Every default rule and fixture will revert to its original configuration, and any that were deleted will be recreated. Custom rules and fixtures are not affected.

guardrails.emptyCore: No prompt core — run the seed
guardrails.helpCost: Costs one model call per draft.
guardrails.ruleDialogHint: The kind decides what is analysed; the severity decides what happens when the rule fails.
guardrails.keyImmutable: The key does not change: it identifies the rule in traces and overrides.
guardrails.kindImmutable: The kind cannot change after creation — the config shape depends on it.
guardrails.promptTextPlaceholder: What the assistant should read in its prompt (optional)
guardrails.promptTextHint: Added to the guardrail layer of the compiled prompt. Empty = runtime-only rule.

deleteConfirm.title: Delete “{label}”?
deleteConfirm.body: This rule will no longer apply. “Reset all” will recreate it if it came from the seed — a hand-written rule, no.

config.criterionPlaceholder: The reply states no fact that is not in the allowed claims.
config.nothingToConfigure: Nothing to configure: this rule only adds its text to the prompt.

errors.invalidConfig: The configuration is invalid for this kind of rule.
errors.customCannotBlock: A “prompt instruction” analyses nothing: marked blocking, it shows as a hard guardrail while it can refuse nothing. To guarantee behaviour, use “Model judgement”.

core.editHint: The shared text injected as L0 into every assistant's prompt.
core.publishWarning: Publishing creates a NEW version: the old one stays intact so history remains readable. Every assistant will need recompiling and re-testing before it can be activated.
core.unchanged: The text is identical to the current version: publishing would stale every assistant without changing anything.

fixtures.hint: An exchange replayed against the assistant: what the client writes, and what the reply must — or must not — do.
fixtures.firstOutboundWarning: No "out" turn: this scenario tests a FIRST outbound message. The CASL identification rule will require naming the organisation in it, and the fixture will fail for a reason unrelated to what it checks.

deleteConfirm.title: Delete “{label}”?
deleteConfirm.body: This scenario will no longer be replayed. “Reset all” will recreate it if it came from the seed.

presets.hint: Pick what the rule should prevent. The configuration is already written.

list.title: AI assistants
list.subtitle: Every assistant is fully editable: goal, tone, tools, guardrails and prompt.

empty.title: No assistants
empty.desc: Create an assistant or import one from a JSON file.

deleteConfirm.title: Delete “{name}”?
deleteConfirm.body: This assistant has never sent a message: it will be permanently deleted.
deleteConfirm.bodyArchive: This assistant has already sent messages. It will be archived, not deleted — conversations must stay readable alongside the assistant that wrote them.

editor.unsavedLeave: You have unsaved changes. Leaving this page will discard them.

stale.title: Stale prompt
stale.body: The configuration changed since the last compile. Settings re-read every turn (tools, model, budgets) already apply; the prompt TEXT is still the one from the last compile.
stale.bodyActive: This assistant is active. Settings re-read every turn already apply to ongoing conversations; the prompt text is still the older one. Recompile to align them.

effects.immediate: {count, plural, one {# setting applies} other {# settings apply}} from the next message
effects.pending: {count, plural, one {# setting is waiting} other {# settings are waiting}} for a recompile

goal.chainNote: A SOFT refusal steps down one rung. A hard refusal never touches the chain: the conversation closes.
goal.noFallbacks: No fallbacks — a postponement ends the follow-up.
goal.whatToObtain: What the assistant is trying to obtain
goal.calendarHint: Decides which CRM appointment type is checked for availability.

knowledge.placeholder: A verifiable fact the assistant may state
knowledge.empty: No allowed claims: the assistant may not state any business information.
knowledge.warning: Anything listed here will be stated in writing on behalf of a licensed broker.

tools.requiredNote: “stop” and “handoff” cannot be disabled: they are how a refusal is honoured and a human is brought in.

guardrails.coreNote: Shared by every assistant. Edit them under Guardrails; here they can only be overridden for this assistant.
guardrails.ownEmpty: No specific rules — the core rules apply alone.

model.toolWarning: This model does not support tools: the assistant will not be able to check the calendar or book.
model.routingNote: These values apply to the router only; direct providers ignore them.

prompt.notCompiled: Not compiled yet — run a compile to see the prompt.
prompt.rawWarning: In free mode the tabs no longer write the prompt. The configuration still drives runtime behaviour.

errors.staleCompile: The prompt must be recompiled before activation.
errors.suiteNotPassed: The guardrail suite must be green before activation.

identity.namedPersonWarning: The assistant writes on behalf of a person but no account is attached: meetings will fall back to an administrator.
identity.freeTextHint: No account linked: meetings will fall back to an administrator.
identity.linkedHint: The name follows the chosen account; meetings are assigned to them.

import.title: Import an assistant
import.bindingsNote: The file comes from another installation: its ids point at nobody here. Pick the local equivalent for each reference.
import.invalid: This file is not a valid assistant export.

goalTypeHint.video_meeting: Books a video call in the calendar.
goalTypeHint.in_person_meeting: Books a meeting at the office or the client's place.
goalTypeHint.phone_call: Books a call slot in the calendar.
goalTypeHint.collect_email: Books nothing: only tries to get an email address.
goalTypeHint.collect_callback_time: Books nothing: agrees on a time to call back.
goalTypeHint.qualify_only: NEVER proposes a meeting — only gathers information.
goalTypeHint.handoff: Books nothing: aims to hand the conversation to a human.

sandbox.disclaimer: Preview: nothing is sent, nothing is saved, no calendar slot is booked. Tool calls are reported, never executed.
sandbox.notCompiled: Compile the assistant before trying it: the sandbox uses the compiled prompt.
sandbox.start: Write what a client might reply, or pick an example:
sandbox.emptyDraft: (no text — the model only called a tool)

triggerHint.inbound: You play the client: write what they would send.
triggerHint.lead_created: The assistant writes the first message, as on an incoming lead.
triggerHint.category_changed: The assistant writes the first message, as after a stage change.

goLive.title: Go live
goLive.subtitle: What has to be true for a real SMS to reach a real number.

ready.title: Ready to send
ready.body: Every blocking condition is met. Messages will really go out.

notReady.title: {count} blocker(s)
notReady.body: While a blocker remains, nothing sends — whatever any other screen says.

mode.label: Send mode
mode.fix: The engine is in dry run. Set SMS_MODE=live to send for real.

live_confirmed.label: Live mode confirmation
live_confirmed.fix: SMS_MODE=live is not enough: add SMS_LIVE_CONFIRMED=true. Two flags, so a deployment inheriting a variable does not start writing.

kill_switch.label: Kill switch
kill_switch.fix: The kill switch is down: nothing sends, whatever the mode. Lift it in the SMS settings.

twilio_credentials.label: Twilio credentials
twilio_credentials.fix: TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID and a token (TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN or TWILIO_API_KEY_SECRET) are required.

webhook_signature.label: Webhook signature
webhook_signature.fix: Without TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN, an inbound message can be forged by anyone.

sms_number.label: Active sending number
sms_number.fix: No active SMS number: there is nowhere to send from. Add one in the settings.

messaging_service.label: Messaging service (A2P)
messaging_service.fix: Active numbers have no Messaging Service: sending works but loses A2P grouping, which is what gets a number flagged.

consented_clients.label: Clients with valid SMS consent
consented_clients.fix: No valid consent: a campaign will enroll nobody. Check that the lead webhook records the ledger.

assistant_active.label: Active assistant
assistant_active.fix: No active assistant: nobody will reply. Compile one, get the suite green, then activate it.

assistant_suite.label: Guardrail suite of active assistants
assistant_suite.fix: An active assistant has a red suite: it was activated bypassing the requirement. Re-run its suite.

campaign_active.label: Active campaign
campaign_active.fix: No active campaign: nobody will be enrolled. Not blocking if you write by hand.

dispatcher.label: Dispatcher
dispatcher.fix: The dispatcher has not beaten for over 15 minutes: messages pile up in the queue without leaving. Check the n8n cron to /api/cron/dispatch.

llm_provider.label: Model provider
llm_provider.fix: No model key configured: the assistant cannot write anything.

model.empty: No model available — check the provider key.
model.effortHint: This model can think before answering. More effort helps on hard decisions but costs tokens and adds latency.

effortDesc.none: Answers directly. Fastest and cheapest — enough for most SMS.
effortDesc.low: Thinks briefly. A good trade-off when the assistant hesitates between two tools.
effortDesc.medium: Thinks more. Useful on conversations that wander.
effortDesc.high: Thinks at length. Can add several seconds before each reply — noticeable in a conversation.

create.title: Create an assistant
create.subtitle: Three ways to get there — all produce a complete configuration.

ai.name: Describe what you need
ai.pitch: Write what you want to achieve. It asks two or three questions, then prepares everything.
ai.title: Describe what you need
ai.subtitle: A few questions, and the configuration is ready to review.
ai.example: For example: "follow up on my old seller leads that have been dormant for months"
ai.noProvider: No model key configured — assisted creation needs a provider.
ai.retry: Unreadable model reply. Rephrase and try again.

simple.name: Simple setup
simple.pitch: Four choices: who you write to, what you want, and how hard to push.
simple.title: Simple setup
simple.subtitle: The four settings that really change behaviour.
simple.goal: What do you want to get?
simple.balancedHint: Two spaced follow-ups. The usual setting.

complex.name: Full setup
complex.pitch: Every setting: goal, tone, knowledge, tools, guardrails, model, prompt.
complex.title: Full setup
complex.subtitle: We create a draft, then you configure everything in the editor.
complex.note: The assistant is created with sensible defaults. You will adjust each tab next.
